test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following was NOT a component of globalisation in India's economic reforms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Promoting local-only trade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The economic reforms in India initiated in 1991 were centered around liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG).
 
• Globalization, as part of these reforms, focused on integrating the Indian economy with the global market to increase trade and economic interdependence.
 
• Promoting "local-only trade" is contrary to the fundamental essence of globalization, which emphasizes international trade and the free movement of goods, services, and investments across borders.
 
• The reforms under globalization included encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI), liberalizing imports, and allowing foreign technology to foster competition and economic growth in India.
 
• Thus, the idea of restricting trade to a local-only framework was not aligned with the objectives of globalization in India's economic reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allowing foreign technology**:

 
 
• Globalization enabled the transfer of advanced technology from developed countries to India, helping to modernize various industries.
 
• Technological collaborations and joint ventures with foreign companies contributed to skill development and innovation in India.
 
• Examples include the entry of global automobile companies and advancements in telecommunications and IT sectors.
 
 
 
• **Encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI)**:
 
 
• FDI played a pivotal role in the globalization process by bringing in foreign capital, boosting industrial growth, and generating employment opportunities.
 
• India opened up several sectors for FDI, including manufacturing, IT, retail, and infrastructure.
 
• FDI also facilitated the integration of Indian companies into global supply chains, enhancing their competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Liberalizing imports**:
 
 
• Reducing trade barriers such as tariffs, duties, and quotas was a critical step in promoting globalization.
 
• Liberalizing imports allowed Indian consumers to access a variety of high-quality goods at competitive prices.
 
• This measure also encouraged domestic industries to improve their efficiency and quality to compete globally.
